residencyRequirements.description: One of the parties must have been a resident of North Carolina for at least six months immediately before filing.

waitingPeriod.description: North Carolina has no waiting period after filing. However, the parties must have lived separate and apart for ONE YEAR before the divorce can be filed. The one-year separation IS the grounds for divorce, not a waiting period after filing.
waitingPeriod.notes: Critical: The one-year separation must be complete BEFORE filing, not after. Divorce cannot be granted until at least one year of separation has occurred.

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart for one year, and one party has been a North Carolina resident for six months immediately before filing.
noFault.notes: This is the ONLY commonly used ground for absolute divorce in North Carolina. The separation must be for at least one year with at least one party intending the separation to be permanent.

noFault.name: Incurable Insanity
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart for five years on account of the incurable insanity of the defendant.
noFault.notes: Rarely used; requires judicial declaration of incurable insanity

groundsForDivorce.note: North Carolina no longer has fault-based grounds for absolute divorce. Fault may be relevant only for alimony claims.

propertyDivision.description: North Carolina is an equitable distribution state. Marital property is presumptively divided equally, but the court may deviate based on 12 statutory factors. CRITICAL: Property distribution must be resolved in a SEPARATE proceeding. A divorce judgment does NOT automatically distribute property. A claim for equitable distribution must be filed BEFORE the divorce is granted or the right is PERMANENTLY WAIVED.
propertyDivision.waiverWarning: Claims for equitable distribution, alimony, and post-separation support MUST be raised before the divorce judgment is entered or they are permanently waived.
factors: Income, property, and liabilities of each party at the time the division of property is to become effective
Obligations for support arising from a prior marriage
Duration of the marriage and age and physical and mental health of both parties
Needs of a parent with custody of a child of the marriage
Expectation of pension, retirement, or other deferred compensation rights
Any equitable claim to, interest in, or direct or indirect contribution made to the acquisition of such marital property by the party not having title
Any direct or indirect contribution made by one spouse to help educate or develop the career potential of the other spouse
Any direct contribution to an increase in value of separate property
Liquid or nonliquid character of all marital property and divisional property
Difficulty of evaluating any component asset or any interest in a business, corporation or profession
Acts of either party to maintain, preserve, develop, or expand; or to waste, neglect, devalue or convert the marital property or divisional property

alimony.description: The court may award alimony or post-separation support to a dependent spouse. Fault (adultery) may affect alimony eligibility. CRITICAL: Alimony must be requested BEFORE the divorce is granted or the right is permanently waived.

postSeparationSupport.description: Temporary support during the period of separation and before the divorce

alimony.waiverWarning: Alimony must be claimed before the divorce judgment is entered.

custody.description: Custody is a separate proceeding from the divorce in North Carolina. The court can award joint or sole legal and physical custody.

childSupport.description: Child support is calculated under North Carolina Child Support Guidelines. It is a separate proceeding from the absolute divorce.

separationAgreement.name: Separation Agreement
separationAgreement.notes: Strongly recommended to resolve property, alimony, and custody before or simultaneously with divorce

filingFees.notes: Approximately $225 in most counties. Additional fees for service. Fee waiver (IFP) available for qualifying individuals.

legalCitations.description: Divorce from bonds of matrimony — one-year separation ground
Divorce for incurable insanity — five-year separation
Equitable distribution of marital and divisional property
Post-separation support — temporary support during separation

formattingRequirements.notes: North Carolina General Court of Justice — District Court Division handles divorce matters.

basic.name: Judgment of Absolute Divorce (AOC-CV-524)
basic.description: Court order granting the absolute divorce

service.name: Acceptance of Service (AOC-CV-644)
service.description: Defendant accepts service without formal process

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet A or B
withChildren.description: Worksheet A for sole custody; Worksheet B for joint/shared custody. Per N.C.G.S. § 50-13.4.

withChildren.name: Financial Affidavit (AOC-CV-627)
withChildren.description: Required disclosure of income and expenses for child support determination

withChildren.name: Custody and Visitation Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing custody and visitation (separate proceeding from divorce)
withChildren.notes: Custody must be filed as a separate action or resolved by agreement before or at the time of divorce

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside North Carolina must file an answer within 30 days of service; additional time may be granted by the court

childSupportGuidelines.description: North Carolina uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined to determine a basic child support obligation from a schedule. The obligation is then apportioned between the parents based on their share of combined income. Adjustments are made for health insurance, childcare, extraordinary expenses, and the number of overnights.

worksheets.worksheetA: Primary custody (sole physical custody) — one parent has 243+ overnights
worksheets.worksheetB: Joint/shared custody — each parent has 123+ overnights
worksheets.worksheetC: Split custody — each parent has primary custody of at least one child

childSupportGuidelines.statute: N.C.G.S. § 50-13.4; North Carolina Child Support Guidelines

options: County where either party resides at the time of filing
